request.input: The supplement company looked at 12 people and found that people who are emotionally triggered should rely on deep breathing alone to calm down.

content.text:
When evaluating information, it is helpful to look at the **scale** and the **source** of the data.

A study of **12 people** is what scientists call a "small sample size." In the world of research, 12 people cannot represent the billions of different human brains and nervous systems. What works for those 12 people may not work for you, because your brain chemistry, your history, and your level of sensitivity are unique.

Furthermore, it is worth noting that a **supplement company** has a financial incentive to promote simple, "natural" wellness tips (like breathing) that align with a general wellness brand, rather than clinical psychological interventions (like DBT).

**Here is the most important thing to consider:**

You are currently experiencing a very specific and painful problem: **you are losing a "disgusting amount of sleep" and it takes you nearly a week to recover from a single comment.**

If the "deep breathing alone" method—which is the most common advice in the world—was the definitive cure for emotional triggers, you would have solved this problem a long time ago. The fact that you are still struggling despite trying deep breathing is the most important piece of evidence you have.

**The difference between "General Advice" and "Personal Solution":**

*   **General Advice (The Blog):** "Deep breathing is good for people who are stressed." (This is generally true).
*   **Personal Solution (Your Life):** "I have tried deep breathing, and I am still losing sleep for 7 days." (This is your reality).

When general advice fails to solve a personal problem, it is time to move from **general** tools to **specialized** tools. 

You don't have to take the word of a supplement company or an online group. You only have to look at your own results. If you want to speed up your recovery process, you deserve to try every tool available—including the ones that might seem "too strong" or "wrong" to others—until you find the one that actually lets you sleep.
